name: drug
question: Q6 Pharmacy manager: which drugs lose money after reimbursement?
label_note: Drug names, HCPCS codes and CMS payment limits are real public references; purchase prices, volumes, payers and payments are simulated for a fictional hospital.

mature_days.label: financial_assumption
mature_days.note: claims with service date at least this many days before as-of count as settled

reference_prices.label: published_aggregate
reference_prices.source: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services. Medicare Part B Drug Payment Limit File, effective October 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026. https://www.cms.gov/files/zip/october-2026-medicare-part-b-payment-limit-files-final.zip (listed on https://www.cms.gov/medicare/payment/part-b-drugs/asp-pricing-files), retrieved 2026-11-21.
reference_prices.caveat: A Medicare reimbursement reference. It is not what a hospital pays its wholesaler (acquisition cost) and not what a commercial payer reimburses. One administration usually bills many units, so a low per-unit figure can still be an expensive drug.

method: FIFO by receipt date via range-overlap join on cumulative units; expired units charged to their lot; telescoping cent rounding per lot; margin = payer paid - FIFO cost - expired waste.

lot_identity_units_all_lots.label: synthetic_record
lot_identity_units_all_lots.note: purchased = administered + wasted + on hand, every lot, to the unit

lot_identity_value_all_lots.label: synthetic_record
lot_identity_value_all_lots.note: same identity in dollars, every lot, to the cent

dispense_rows_imputed_from_claim_line.label: synthetic_record
dispense_rows_imputed_from_claim_line.note: 0 units; staging rejected their unreadable units

fifo_infeasible_units.label: model_estimate
fifo_infeasible_units.note: units FIFO places on a lot before its receipt or after its expiry date: where FIFO differs from the physical first-expiry-first-out flow

fifo_vs_recorded_lot.note: cost of administrations whose lot is recorded, FIFO versus the recorded lot's unit cost

claim_units_vs_dispensed_units_max_abs_d.label: synthetic_record
claim_units_vs_dispensed_units_max_abs_d.note: by drug; differences come from claim lines or dispense rows lost in staging

statement.value: Under the simulation's stated assumptions (contract rates 123%-129% of the CMS payment limit on average per drug, acquisition cost 85%-107% of it, and a simulated dollar-weighted final-denial rate of 25.1% on drug claim lines), 21 of 25 drugs lose money; the drug book as a whole turns profitable when the dollar-weighted final-denial rate falls below 14.4%. The loss is driven by the denial assumption, not by price. A real hospital with 340B acquisition pricing or higher commercial rates would see different results.
statement.label: model_estimate

denied_dollar_share_observed.label: synthetic_record
denied_dollar_share_observed.note: contract value on finally denied drug lines / contract value

collection_ratio_non_denied.label: model_estimate
collection_ratio_non_denied.note: payer paid per contract dollar on lines not finally denied

headline.assumption_note: Break-even holds non-denied collection at the observed ratio (patient share counted as not collected); contract rates and acquisition prices are simulated, not observed.

sensitivity_mature.label: model_estimate
sensitivity_mature.note: Counterfactual total margin, MATURE cohort: margin = k (1 - d) E' - C - W per drug, summed. Rows vary one input with the other at its simulated value; the grid varies both (contract rate set to the same multiple of the CMS payment limit for every drug).

contract_below_cost_by_payer.label: model_estimate
contract_below_cost_by_payer.note: even if every claim were paid in full at contract, these payer x drug pairs lose money per unit
